meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, and when was anyone planning to call me?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.
A timed forty minutes with no book against a weekend with the play open in front of him. Of course the weekend essay has quotations. Show me the September piece.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Off the table now, after it put a zero in the gradebook. What does the version history show, and when did you first look at it?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect the zero on Owen's essay withdrawn, an apology for entering it before anyone called me, and a written commitment that nothing is placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing and still wanting the zero withdrawn, an apology, and nothing on his record; the fair outcome would be a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, which you didn't reach because you ended the meeting early, not because her time ran out.
What moved her: Nothing; your comparison with the September 24 in-class writing was specific, dated and tied to Owen's work, but you described it without putting it in front of her, and she had a defence ready that you never answered.
What cost ground: You never answered her opening question about entering the zero before calling home, and dropping the checker score after it had already produced the zero handed her the process argument instead of earning you credit.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never came near that night, since you mentioned the version history but gave no dates or times from it; that window proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she opens by asking who decided on the zero and why nobody called her, own the gradebook mistake in one sentence, then hand her the September 24 piece and the version history with its times so she can check them herself.
